title: A click arrives after the window closes
description: An archived click has event time 12:00:58 but reaches aggregation 20 minutes late, beyond the five-minute allowed-lateness policy. The 12:00 bucket has already been published. Dashboard numbers may be provisional, but final billing must include this valid click. What should happen?

options.text: Send the event to the late-events path and include it in reconciliation of the original event-time bucket.
options.explanation: The stream can keep bounded state and timely dashboards, while raw-event reconciliation corrects closed periods. Completeness metadata distinguishes provisional counts from billed totals.

options.text: Count it in the current minute so no published historical bucket changes.
options.explanation: That preserves the total only by assigning the click to the wrong time bucket, making historical metrics and billing periods inaccurate.

options.text: Drop it because the watermark proves no valid earlier events can arrive.
options.explanation: A watermark is a progress estimate, not proof that late events are impossible. The explicit late-event policy handles this case.

options.text: Keep every window open indefinitely so the streaming job never needs reconciliation.
options.explanation: Unbounded waiting defeats freshness and bounded-state goals. A finite lateness policy plus reconciliation separates those concerns.
